thread:
incident-bot: P0 Pager — serving-runtime: model-init failures in us-west-2 (prod). Alerts: multiple load OOMs, CUDA errors, and container restarts. Investigate: /incidents/INC-2026-0426 link.

sara: seeing spikes in model-load failures from the warmup queue, ~15 failures in last 10m. Affected: model-id=redwood/large-v3 and quant variants. Logs show OOM during `load_weights`.

jordan: I’m on call, taking this. first pass: are these all on the same node pool? @ops-oncall can you confirm node flaps?

ops-oncall: yes, five restarts in gw-usw2-gpupool-3 around 12:10-12:18 UTC. kube events show `oom_kill` on sidecar and `containerd` restarts.

maya: grabbing `kubectl` logs for one of the failing pods: `kubectl -n inference logs load-warmup-78x9 -c runtime`

maya: logs snippet: ```
2026-04-26T12:11:05Z ERROR runtime: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
2026-04-26T12:11:05Z ERROR model: failed to allocate KV cache, aborting init
2026-04-26T12:11:05Z WARN model-loader: deserialization mismatch, expected 12345678 bytes, got 12345000
```

leo: deserialization mismatch + cuda OOM looks like partial artifact corruption during fetch. Any recent artifact uploads or GC in the registry?

ashley: we rotated the artifact storage credentials yesterday and restarted the artifact-proxy service at 04:00 UTC. registry logs show a few `ConnectionReset` errors during large blob transfers around 11:50 UTC.

jordan: ok hypothesis: incomplete/corrupted model artifact + memory pressure triggers OOM during warmup. Immediate mitigation: 1) divert warmup traffic off gw-usw2-gpupool-3 2) pin serving to older artifact checksum 3) fall back new requests to smaller model variant.

jordan: @deploy-bot please push traffic-policy `route: avoid: gw-usw2-gpupool-3` to the router.

deploy-bot: Executing policy update. Rolling update started. 3/3 routers updated.

ops-oncall: scaling up gpupool-2 by +2 nodes to absorb spilled load. `gcloud compute instances create ...` started. Estimated ready ~5m.

maya: meanwhile I’ll disable pre-warm for the large model to avoid immediate replays: `PATCH /api/v1/models/redwood/large-v3/config {"prewarm": false}` — request applied.

sara: support: please open a high-priority banner for customers using `model: large-v3` with degradation timeframe. list likely-affected customers: fintech-prod-a, retention-search, chat-saas-ops.

ashley: trying to reproduce artifact corruption: fetching blob SHA from registry and verifying size. `curl -I https://artifacts.internal/redwood/large-v3/weights.blob` -> `Content-Length: 12345000` (mismatch). fetching again returns 12345678. suggests intermittent truncation.

leo: run checksum compare locally on one node that successfully loaded: `sha256sum weights.blob` -> `abc123...`; compare to failing node artifact -> truncated file.

jordan: short-term patch: mark the artifact as 'unstable' and force-serving to use replica with validated checksum. ops: quarantine nodes that fetched truncated blob (cordon + drain).

ops-oncall: cordoned gw-usw2-gpupool-3 nodes 3/3. Draining ongoing; migrated 7 pods.

maya: implemented a temporary registry nginx buffer increase to avoid truncation in large transfers and restarted artifact-proxy. config: `client_body_buffer_size 16M` -> `64M`.

ashley: registry metrics show transfer errors tailing off after restart. artifact integrity checker job kicked off to re-validate all recent uploads.

jordan: customer impact: partial degradation for customers pinned to `large-v3` during 12:10-12:30 UTC. Error rate peaked at 12:12 (approx 8% of requests returned 500/timeout during warmup). No data exfiltration. Support ticket created: INC-2026-0426-01.

sara: recommend follow-ups: 1) add artifact transfer checksum validation on-the-fly (fail early) 2) expand warmup retry/backoff with checksum re-fetch 3) add alert for `deserialization mismatch` log pattern.

leo: will file infra PR for `on-download` checksum verification + abort if mismatch. Also adding a short-circuit to avoid allocating GPU memory until artifact validated.

jordan: for now incident status -> Mitigated. Action items assigned: leo (artifact validation PR), maya (postmortem draft + timeline), ashley (registry hardening), ops-oncall (node audit + redeploy drained nodes), sara (customer comms).

incident-bot: Incident status updated to `Mitigated`. Duration: 00:28. Pager closed.

sara: thanks all. Maya — include snippet of truncated bytes and dig into why nginx/proxy produced truncation. Add playbook note: when `deserialization mismatch` occurs, mark artifact unstable and fail fast. :memo:

maya: will do. saving logs to /incidents/INC-2026-0426/artifacts and starting postmortem doc now.

jordan: closing thread here, will update once postmortem is ready. :thumbsup:
